claim: You can enable MFA for the root user and for IAM users, and AWS supports three MFA types: passkeys and security keys (FIDO), virtual authenticator applications (TOTP) and hardware TOTP tokens; AWS recommends phishing-resistant passkeys and security keys.

evidence.quote: AWS supports the following MFA types for your root user:
You can enable MFA for the AWS account root user of all AWS accounts, including standalone accounts, management accounts, and member accounts, as well as for your IAM users.
AWS supports the following MFA types:
evidence.heading: MFA types

evidence.quote: AWS Identity and Access Management supports passkeys and security keys for MFA.
Virtual authenticator apps implement the [time-based one-time password (TOTP) algorithm](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6238) and support multiple tokens on a single device.
For instructions on setting up a hardware TOTP token for an IAM user, see Assign a hardware TOTP token in the AWS Management Console.

We recommend that you use phishing-resistant MFA such as passkeys and security keys whenever possible. These FIDO-based authenticators use public key cryptography and are resistant to phishing, man-in-the-middle, and replay attacks, providing a stronger level of security than TOTP-based options.
